To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Pax proteins play a central role in the assembly of gene regulatory networks that orchestrate the production of neuronal diversity.

Pax proteins act as transcription factors that control neuronal diversity and that Pax6 plays an essential role in orchestrating the emergence of neuronal subtypes in a spatio-temporal manner during development.
Pax proteins are key players in neural development and are involved in a wide variety of molecular and cellular processes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms by which transcription factors orchestrate cell fate decisions during the assembly of neural circuits.
the molecular and cellular mechanisms that control the number and diversity of neurons produced during brain development.
the molecular and cellular basis of the development and evolution of the vertebrate nervous system, particularly in the context of sensory organs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Pax proteins are key players in the generation and assembly process of neural circuits.
Pax proteins are key components of gene regulatory networks that orchestrate the emergence of neuronal cell diversity.
the Pax family of transcription factors is a major player in the generation of neuronal diversity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Pax proteins are key players in orchestrating the generation and differentiation of neuronal cells, and that Pax6 is the master regulator of this process.

Pax proteins, through their interactions with other transcription factors, chromatin modifiers and signaling pathways, orchestrate the emergence of neuronal subtypes and pace the emergence of neural diversity during development.
Pax proteins act as a central hub within regulatory networks, orchestrating and timing the emergence of neuronal subtypes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the molecular and cellular properties of Pax proteins are not only important in the generation of neural diversity but also in the coordination of the emergence of neural diversity.
Pax proteins, and Pax6 in particular, are not just transcription factors that regulate the expression of other genes.
Pax proteins are key players in the generation and assembly, in time and space, of neural circuits during development.
